As Alibaba Group Hldg LTD (BABA) Shares Rose, Shareholder Whale Rock Capital Management Has Lowered Position; Honeywell International (HON) Shareholder Saturna Capital Boosted Holding by $720,000
June 10, 2018 - By Marie Mckinney
Saturna Capital Corp increased its stake in Honeywell International (HON) by 1.66% based on its latest 2018Q1 regulatory filing with the SEC. Saturna Capital Corp bought 5,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.73% with the market. The institutional investor held 306,856 shares of the o.e.m. company at the end of 2018Q1, valued at $44.34M, up from 301,856 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Saturna Capital Corp who had been investing in Honeywell International for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $113.43B market cap company. The stock decreased 0.15% or $0.23 during the last trading session, reaching $151.86. About 1.94 million shares traded. Honeywell International Inc. (NYSE:HON) has risen 12.64% since June 10, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 0.07% the S&P500. Alex Sacerdote decreased its stake in Alibaba Group Hldg Ltd (BABA) by 19.52% based on its latest 2018Q1 regulatory filing with the SEC. Whale Rock Capital Management Llc sold 180,096 shares as the company’s stock rose 2.58% while stock markets declined. The hedge fund run by Alex Sacerdote held 742,333 shares of the business services company at the end of 2018Q1, valued at $136.25M, down from 922,429 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Whale Rock Capital Management Llc who had been investing in Alibaba Group Hldg Ltd for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $526.92B market cap company. The stock increased 0.71% or $1.45 during the last trading session, reaching $205.07. About 17.53 million shares traded. Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA) has risen 61.13% since June 10, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 48.56% the S&P500. Analysts await Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE:BABA) to report earnings on August, 16. They expect $1.16 earnings per share, up 23.40% or $0.22 from last year’s $0.94 per share. BABA’s profit will be $2.98 billion for 44.20 P/E if the $1.16 EPS becomes a reality. After $0.54 actual earnings per share reported by Alibaba Group Holding Limited for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts 114.81% EPS growth.
